evidence.reason: Confirmed from the pinned source. The dispatch wrapper performs fallback provider admission before payload preparation, and its own comment states the intended rule: a lane 'must observe its provider's persisted cooldown (recorded below by remember_provider_limit) instead of reopening the rate-limited lane'. The final launch boundary inside _dispatch, reached only after worktree retention and the snapshot/review-diff secret scans, rechecks just the wall-clock deadline (lines 451-458) and GLM blackout (459-460) before the driver switch (461-468); it never re-reads the selected provider's persisted cooldown. So a cooldown persisted by another worker (CRQ runs concurrent runners/signers) while worker A scans is not observed and a paid call can start against an already rate-limited provider. This is an implementation error in existing, code-documented intended behavior, not a new requirement: it is the exact preparation-time TOCTOU class the codebase already fixed for deadline and blackout (comment lines 442-450; history 'charge payload preparation to the shared dispatch deadline'), with the provider-cooldown dimension left unenforced at the same boundary. Smallest compatible fix: re-read the selected provider's persisted cooldown at this boundary and, if active, return a deferral the fallback loop treats as provider-unavailable without recording a new provider rate-limit event. Routine correctness repair, no disruptive behavior change or architectural rework, so no owner judgment is needed. The finding's cited admission-read line (~321) lies outside the visible excerpt, but the dispatch comment plus the verified boundary code establish the mechanics; nothing in the contract retires fallback cooldown admission, and no commit in history fixes it.
